transcript.text:
I can help with that. To narrow this down quickly, I need to know exactly what happens when you try to use it. 1. Does the machine not start at all (no lights, no sound), or does it run but just doesn't dry?
2. When you turn it on, do any lights come up on the display?
3. Is the door firmly closed? Some machines won't start if they think the door is open. Please let me know these details so I can guide you to the right fix.
Lights come on but when I press start nothing happens, no sound at all. Door doesn't seem to close properly, it's been loose for a few days.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door handle / catch (mechanical). Check the dryer's plug is pushed fully in and the socket is on, and try another appliance in that socket. If the house electrics have tripped, don't keep resetting it. Was a switch, plug or fuse off (and is it sorted), or does the socket work fine with something else?
Plug is in and the socket's on, the lights come on so it's getting power. Fuse box is fine too.
Open the door, make sure no clothing is caught in it, then shut it firmly until it clicks and press start. Does it still show the door as open?

It won't click shut, the door swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door firmly shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The checks point to the door handle. To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint. I don't know the model number offhand, I'll go and look inside the door recess and tell you.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The checks point to the door handle. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I haven't got the number yet, I don't know it offhand. Do you definitely need it, or can you tell me what's wrong with the door first?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Yes, the model number is essential because Hotpoint tumble dryers have different safety mechanisms and part specifications. Without knowing the exact model, I cannot confirm if a simple repair kit will work or if the entire door assembly needs replacing. With the dryer unplugged, look at the catch on the door and the slot it clicks into: fluff or a bit of fabric can stop it engaging, and check the door lines up when you close it. Is the catch broken, was something stopping it (now cleared), or does it all look fine?
The catch is broken, the plastic tongue on the door snapped off and I found the piece on the floor. Nothing was blocking it. I'll go and get the model number now if you still need it.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The evidence is clear: the plastic tongue on the door has snapped off. This is a mechanical failure of the door handle/catch assembly. The safety interlock switch inside the frame never gets triggered, so the dryer will not start unless you hold it shut. You need to replace the door handle and catch mechanism. Since you do not have the model number yet, please find it on the sticker inside the door recess or on the back of the machine when you can reach it. You will need that exact model number to order the correct part from a spare parts retailer (search for 'Hotpoint tumble dryer door handle' plus your model). 1. Unplug the dryer.
2. Remove the old broken plastic pieces.
3. Fit the new handle/catch assembly according to the instructions that come with it.
4. Plug it back in and test. If you are unsure about fitting the part or if the door frame itself is cracked, please call a qualified engineer.

Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that.
